candidate_only.reason: Present only in the withdrawn 0.3.0 candidate (2e765e2). Never published, so removing it carries no public compatibility debt. File-first consent replaces it.

confluence page copy.reason: Verified client-side page copy; kept in the target surface for run-owned validation copies.

accept_conversion.reason: Requires the exact returned source-conversion fingerprint before a lossy create.

asset_dir.note: Local image support. A Markdown body writing ![](diagram.png) had no way to publish that file: these commands had no notion of a local file, so the reference shipped as a broken link. Optional -- omitted, references resolve from the body file's own directory, and a body from stdin with a local reference is refused with this flag named rather than resolved against whatever the shell's working directory happened to be.

confluence page create.reason: Markdown writes use source-bound informed-consent preflight.

confluence page diff-local.reason: Hidden from help and completion; behaviour, options, exit codes and JSON unchanged.
confluence page diff-local.visibility_reason: Hidden from help and completion in favour of the `md`/`xhtml` workflow groups. The command, its options, its exit codes and its JSON are unchanged and scripts keep working -- but two documented names for one command is the confusion the grouping was added to remove, so only one is documented. Returned `next_actions` name the visible spelling.

confluence page diff-xhtml.reason: The escape hatch for pages Markdown cannot hold. The low-level read and write already existed -- 'page get --body-repr=storage' and 'page update --body-format=storage' -- and everything around them did not, so guidance to use XHTML left callers composing commands out of parts of an error message. What the server holds now against what is on disk, plus the candidate hash a publish takes.

confluence page finalize-merge.reason: Rebinds a reviewed merge to the current remote as a document push-md accepts. prepare-merge writes plain Markdown so an agent can read and edit it, and push-md takes only a managed document -- without this the workflow ended one step short of the thing it exists for: the merged text was there and nothing could publish it. Rewriting the manifest is the one part of a merge that must not be done by hand, and it writes a new file rather than the canonical one, because until the push succeeds nothing has been published.

passthrough_prefix.reason: Canonical repeatable prefix allowlist for readable Markdown conversion.

confluence page get.reason: Readable Markdown can preserve explicitly selected HTML-comment prefixes.

confluence page inspect.reason: Read-only page diagnostics and workflow recommendation surface.

confluence page md.reason: Workflow group. The names existed but the shape did not: `get`/`update` are single actions while the managed Markdown and storage paths are workflows, and nothing in the naming said which was which. The same function objects are registered under both spellings, so there is one implementation and the two cannot drift. Old names keep working.

confluence page md compare.reason: The single canonical comparison command, and three-way: base, local file and page, so a remote edit made since the pull shows up here instead of being discovered by a refused push. Read-only in both directions -- PUT 0, and no canonical file written unless --write-workspace names a directory. `--view=diff` renders the same comparison as text; the 0.4.0 `md diff` alias is withdrawn because it pointed at `diff-local`, which compares against the base and cannot see a remote edit at all.

confluence page md finalize-merge.reason: Alias of `finalize-merge`. Visible: `merge_available` and `prepare-merge` emit it as a `next_actions` argv, and an action the product tells a caller to run has to be one `--help` admits exists.

confluence page md prepare-merge.reason: Alias of `prepare-merge`. Visible: `merge_available` and `prepare-merge` emit it as a `next_actions` argv, and an action the product tells a caller to run has to be one `--help` admits exists.

confluence page md prepare-reconcile.reason: Lays base, local and remote out in a run-owned directory with a report. Writes only inside that directory; the canonical file is untouched. Replaces prepare-merge, which stays as a hidden alias for one release.

confluence page md rebaseline.reason: The narrow escape from manifest_base_projection_mismatch: the binding checks out and the recorded base hash is still not what this converter produces. PUT 0, body unchanged, and it requires the approval fingerprint of a comparison the caller reviewed. The next push performs the full proof with no waiver.

confluence page md record-reconciled-aga.reason: Rebinds a reconciled body to the remote it was reconciled against. PUT 0. The only step in the stale flow that may replace a canonical body, and it refuses unless a fresh read still produces the fingerprint the comparison did -- so a page that moved or a file edited meanwhile ends in a named refusal. Replaces finalize-merge, which stays as a hidden alias.

confluence page md validate.reason: Alias of `validate-local`; it validates a managed Markdown file.

confluence page patch-text.reason: Exact plain-text leaf patch; the canonical low-cost edit path in the target model.

confluence page prepare-merge.reason: Lays out base, local and remote as three files so a stale edit can be merged by the party that reads documents for meaning. Measured across 55 live pages, every managed push against a page someone else had touched stopped at the refusal with nothing to do but redo the edit by hand. Reads the page and writes local files; it never publishes.

no_assets.reason: Explicitly records referenced attachments as verified remote-only manifest entries.

confluence page pull-batch.reason: Batch pull keeps the existing command while adopting the same portable manifest and asset materialization contract as pull-md.
confluence page pull-batch.visibility_reason: Hidden from help and completion in favour of the `md`/`xhtml` workflow groups. The command, its options, its exit codes and its JSON are unchanged and scripts keep working -- but two documented names for one command is the confusion the grouping was added to remove, so only one is documented. Returned `next_actions` name the visible spelling.

accept_migration.reason: A page whose grade forbids the canonical write now writes nothing; this approves the named losses of a migration_required page by the exact fingerprint of the report the refusal printed. Scoped to that one grade on purpose -- 8.2 declines to add a plain --force, and a flag that unlocked every forbidden grade would be one.

no_assets.reason: Explicitly records referenced attachments as verified remote-only manifest entries.

write_base_cache.reason: The full base Markdown sidecar is no longer written by default: the v3 manifest is the only required persistent metadata and the merge base comes from the page history it names. This flag asks for the cache anyway, for offline or retention use. Existing sidecars are still read.

confluence page pull-md.reason: --output becomes required; readable stdout moves to `page get --body-repr=md`.
confluence page pull-md.visibility_reason: Hidden from help and completion in favour of the `md`/`xhtml` workflow groups. Publishes only the exact bytes named by --accept-candidate: a storage document can be edited between the dry run that was reviewed and the push that publishes.

confluence page recover-assets.reason: Uploads the pictures a page is missing, without touching its body. A create whose uploads did not all land could not be recovered by rerunning the write: after a create the page body already is the candidate, so the update returns no_change and never reaches the uploads. Missing means no attachment with that filename -- not a claim that two files are the same, but that the reference resolves, which is what was broken. Idempotent by consequence: a second run uploads nothing.

confluence page set-authority.reason: Declares which representation may publish a page. Without it, Markdown and storage can both publish the same page and the conflict this design set out to remove returns under a new name. Takes the files as well as the id because nothing here maps an id to the documents pulled from it.

accept_migration.reason: Requires the exact source-bound migration fingerprint before a lossy update.

asset_dir.note: Local image support. A Markdown body writing ![](diagram.png) had no way to publish that file: these commands had no notion of a local file, so the reference shipped as a broken link. confluence page validate-local.reason: Offline managed-file validation; rewritten file-first in Story 5-7 but the command stays.

confluence page validate-xhtml.reason: The escape hatch for pages Markdown cannot hold. Offline parse, namespace and identity check: the failures worth catching here are the ones an editor introduces, and none of them need a round trip.

doctor.reason: Gains an opt-in flag; every pre-existing parameter and default is untouched.

jira issue description.note: Exposed in 0.3.4, all at once. A description workflow that can pull but not publish, or publish but not recover, invites a caller to build on a half whose other half has no safe answer -- so the whole set was kept hidden until the acceptance ran: five wiki->md->wiki cycles reaching a fixed point, unsupported input writing nothing, a proven candidate matching what was sent and what came back, and each refusal named separately. Verified offline and against a live sandbox issue.

comment_format.reason: `worklog add` has accepted `--comment-format md` since it was written and this took the comment raw, so the same Markdown published as a transition comment and as a worklog note produced two different things on the issue. The difference tracked where the two commands were written, not anything about comments.

jira issue transition.reason: Transition comments take the same format contract as every other Jira comment.

setup uninstall.reason: Removes atls-installed skill files and routing blocks; --state performs legacy local-state cleanup without opening a SQLite runtime.

system_certs.reason: Opt-in pass-through of `uv tool upgrade --system-certs` for TLS-inspecting corporate proxies. Never appended automatically — older uv builds reject the flag.

note: Plan 4.4 makes v0.2.13 the public compatibility baseline: anything not listed here
must stay byte-identical in the CLI surface.
'candidate_only' lists surface that exists in the withdrawn 0.3.0 candidate (2e765e2)
but is absent from both v0.2.13 and the target, so it is neither a baseline delta nor
an addition; Story 11 deletes it. Tracking it separately keeps the gate honest while
the withdrawn candidate is still checked out.
